map.An Axiom City episode — Lessons 2-1 & 2-: An Axiom City episode. Lessons 2-1 & 2-2 in one go. It has three reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Pattern distortion detected, crew. It is: I see a glitch in the patterns, crew. It is shaped like a clipboard.
map.Previously: on a rained-out field day, f: Before: it was a rainy field day. Four sixth graders opened Ada Vex's shut book. It was in old Vexhall. They woke VEX, a part of her Pattern Engine. Now the city's patterns are their problem.
map.Founders Festival, day one. Morning. A f: It's day one of Founders Festival. It's morning. A new poster. It is still warm from the census printer.
map.By order of the census office: the OFFIC: This form is OFFICIAL. It is from the census office. It is for the fair. Answer it. Do not question it.
It's a form made of questions, Mr. Pimm. We are meant to question it.
map.Distortion source confirmed: the form it: I found where the glitch comes from: the form. Its questions can not measure real things. Crew, read the machine. Do it before it reads you.
map.Under the notice board. Theo has been sq: Under the board. Theo squints. It has been three whole minutes.
map.Half of these questions could be answere: A sign could answer half of these questions. "What time does the parade start?" — Ask a hundred visitors. You get ONE answer. That is just a fact.
map.But \"How many napkins does each visitor: But "How many napkins does each visitor grab?" — Not all people grab the same. THAT one would measure a real thing.
map.Definition loaded: a statistical questio: New word: a statistical question expects answers that VARY. Each person may give a new answer. A one-answer question? It is just a fact with a question mark.
map.A statistical question anticipates varie: A statistical question gets lots of answers. "How many napkins does each visitor grab?" — It has many answers. "What time does the parade start?" — It has just one.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. S: Reader, you are crew member five. Sort Pimm's form. Which questions can measure this fair?
map.Four questions from Pimm's official form: Four questions from Pimm's form. Tag each one: STATISTICAL (answers vary) or ONE ANSWER (a single fact).
map.Conceptual: a statistical question antic: Conceptual: a statistical question expects answers that VARY. Ask it to 100 visitors. You would get lots of answers. A fact question gets the same answer. It does not matter who you ask.
map.Procedural: test each line — 'Would two: Procedural: test each line — 'Would two visitors give two different answers?' — What each visitor buys changes from person to person. So does how long each one waits. The year it began never changes. The count of gates never changes.
map.Harbor Row, mid-morning. Lines everywher: Harbor Row, mid-morning. Lines all over. Dev has a stopwatch and a job.
map.Side quest complete: I timed how long ei: Side quest done: I timed eighteen visitors in line. Eighteen data points. Raw loot.
map.Raw numbers are mush. I could build that: Raw numbers are a mess. I could build them into bars. A histogram.
map.Histogram schema: sort data into equal i: Histogram plan: sort data into equal intervals (bins). Each bar's height = the frequency. That is how many values land in that bin. Bars touch. No gaps.
map.A histogram shows how often data falls i: A histogram: how often data falls in each interval. Height = frequency. The bars touch, since the intervals do.
map.Bar heights, reader — stack the eighteen: Bar heights, reader. Stack the eighteen waits. Make bars Pimm can't argue with!
map.Dev's log — minutes each of 18 visitors:
Dev's log: how many minutes each of 18 visitors waited in line:
4 · 12 · 25 · 17 · 8 · 21 · 14 · 27 · 11 · 6 · 19 · 23 · 15 · 28 · 13 · 22 · 10 · 20
Count how many waits land in each bin. Then set the three bar heights.
map.Conceptual: each bar's height is a FREQU: Conceptual: each bar's height is a FREQUENCY. It counts the waits in that interval. There are 18 waits. Each wait lands in exactly one bin.
map.Procedural: go wait by wait and tick a b: Procedural: go wait by wait. Tick a bin: 4→(0–9), 12→(10–19), 25→(20–29)… Your three counts must add up to 18.
map.My churro line is in there somewhere. Lo: My churro line is in there. Look at it. The fair has a shape at last.
map.Pretty bars, children. But where is the: Pretty bars, kids. But where is the TYPICAL wait? Your chart does not even list the numbers now!
map.It doesn't have to list them. The bars r: It does not need to list them. The bars keep how many. And how many is enough.
map.Pimm produces a rule book. The crew prod: Pimm brings out a rule book. The crew brings out better thinking.
map.Observation: ordered readings stack bin: Look: readings in order stack bin by bin. This test board has bins of 2, 5 and 3. Where is the 5th reading? Bin one holds #1–2. Bin two holds #3–7. The 5th is in bin two.
map.It's a minimap. You don't see every enem: It's like a small game map. You don't see each enemy. You see where they group up. Count up the bars. Then you can point at ANY spot.
map.Bar heights add up in order: the first b: Bar heights add up in order. The first bar holds the smallest readings. The next bar goes on with the count. Add frequencies left to right. Then you can find any spot in the data. You do not need the list.
Noon at the board. A crowd. A clerk. A challenge.
map.Eighteen waits, and your precious raw li: Eighteen waits, and your raw list is gone. Find me the middle of the line: the 9th and 10th waits. Use the BARS alone. You can't.
Reader, read the histogram. Call it.
map.Boss Gate: the bins hold 3, then 8, then: Boss Gate: the bins hold 3, then 8, then 7 of the 18 waits. Stack the counts in order. The histogram will show you the middle.
map.BOSS GATE. Two locks. One smug clerk. (N: BOSS GATE. Two locks. One smug clerk. (No stress. Some stress.)
map.Pimm's challenge. Your histogram of 18 w: Pimm's challenge. Your histogram of 18 waits: 0–9 min: 3 waits · 10–19 min: 8 · 20–29 min: 7. The raw list is gone. Two locks:
map.Line the 18 waits up shortest to longest: Line up the 18 waits, short to long. Which bin holds the 9th and 10th waits? That is the middle of the data.
map.Conceptual: a histogram remembers HOW MA: Conceptual: a histogram keeps HOW MANY waits each interval has. They are in order. The short bin is first. Add the bar counts left to right. That shows which interval holds any spot: 1st, 9th, 18th.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: the first bar holds: Procedural: Lock 1: the first bar holds waits #1–3. Add the next bar's height. See which spots IT covers. Then check where the 9th and 10th land. Lock 2: add up each bar's height. Use bars at 10 minutes or more.
map.The office will… revise the form. With q: The office will… fix the form. With questions that, ahem, vary. Churro, anyone? I'll pay.
map.One poster down. But a good question onl: One poster down. But a good question only STARTS the data. Someone still has to find its middle.
map.New distortion humming. It lives in the: A new glitch hums. It lives in the exact middle. To be continued…
map.Statistical question.Expects answers tha: Statistical question.Its answers vary from one person to the next. So it can measure things. A one-answer question is just a fact.
map.Histogram.Equal intervals (bins); bar he: Histogram.Equal intervals (bins). Bar height = frequency. That is how many values land in it. Bars touch, since the intervals do.
map.Reading the bars.Frequencies add up in o: Reading the bars.Frequencies add up in order. Stack bar counts left to right. You can find any spot. Even the middle pair. You do not need the raw list.
map.\"A machine that asks nothing real can m: "Ask no real thing? Then a machine can't measure a real thing. Fix the question first." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 2 · Episode 1: The Questi: completed Unit 2 · Episode 1: The Question Machine. They know statistical questions and histograms.
map.Thank you for reading with the crew. Epi: Thank you for reading with the crew. Episode 2 is next. It waits in the middle.
map.A different poster asks: 'How many seeds: A new poster asks: 'How many seeds are in each fair pumpkin?' — Seed counts change from pumpkin to pumpkin → statistical.
map.'How many letters are in the word FESTIV: 'How many letters are in the word FESTIVAL?' — One set count. Who counts does not matter → NOT statistical.
map.The test is variability — not whether th: The test is variability. It is not if the answer is a number. Both answers are numbers. Only one varies.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.A form has 5 questions; 2 of them have a: A form has 5 questions. 2 of them have answers that vary. How many are statistical?
map.Different log — minutes at the face-pain: A new log: minutes at the face-paint booth: 3, 11, 7, 14, 2, 9, 12, 6. Bins: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14.
map.Check the total: 2 + 3 + 3 = 8 values. A: Check the total: 2 + 3 + 3 = 8 values. All the data is counted. No gaps between bars.
map.In that worked log, how tall is the 5–9: In that log, how tall is the 5–9 bar?
map.Different board: 10 readings in bins of: A new board: 10 readings in bins of 2, 5 and 3. Where is the middle pair? That is the 5th and 6th readings.
map.Count up in order: bin one holds reading: Count up in order: bin one holds readings #1–2. Bin two holds readings #3–7. So bin two has the 5th AND 6th.
map.Count for 'bin two or higher': 5 + 3 = 8: Count for 'bin two or higher': 5 + 3 = 8 readings. The bars always keep how many.
map.On that board (bins 2, 5, 3), how many r: Look at that board (bins 2, 5, 3). How many readings are in the LAST bin alone?
map.Tag all four questions first — every lin: Tag all four questions first. Each line on the form.
map.Sorted! Churros bought and minutes waite: Sorted! Churros bought vary from visitor to visitor. So do minutes waited. Those can measure the fair. The year it began is a single fact. So is the gate count. Pimm's machine asked half its questions to a sign.
map.All 18 waits stacked — and the festival': All 18 waits are stacked. The wait times have a shape at last. Pimm can't argue with it.
map.Pick a bin for Lock 1 first — Pimm is ta: Pick a bin for Lock 1 first. Pimm is tapping his pen.
map.Lock 1 holds. The first bar holds only 3: Lock 1 holds. The first bar holds only 3 waits: spots #1, #2 and #3. Can the 9th wait fit in there?
map.Lock 1 holds. Count up in order: how man: Lock 1 holds. Count up in order. How many waits come BEFORE the 20–29 bar starts?
map.Lock 1 holds. A histogram hides the exac: Lock 1 holds. A histogram hides the exact values. But it still COUNTS in order. The first bar covers spots #1–3. Where does the count go next?
map.Lock 2 holds. Two bars cover 'ten minute: Lock 2 holds. Two bars cover 'ten minutes or more'. Add their heights.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Positions #4–11 fill the: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Spots #4–11 fill the 10–19 bin. The middle pair is there too: 9th and 10th. And 8 + 7 = 15 waits are ten minutes or more. The Question Machine is out of order!
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
map.Walk the steps above again — you've got: Go over the steps above again. You can do this.
